issues.description: Method Stock.take(String): the problem statement UML (problem_statement.md) declares take(String) to return int (using -1 to indicate failure). The solution implementation (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Stock.java) defines take(String) to return int and uses -1 for failure. The template implementation (template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Stock.java) declares take(String) to return boolean and returns true/false. This return-type mismatch prevents students from implementing SealSaloon methods that rely on the int contract (e.g., checking for -1) and will cause compilation or logical errors.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template's Stock.take(String) method signature to return int (matching the UML and solution). Update the template implementation to return -1 when the ingredient is not found or out of stock, and otherwise return the remaining quantity after decrementing by one. Also update any template code that used the boolean return to handle the int contract (e.g., callers should check for -1 to detect failure).

issues.description: Method return-type mismatch for Stock.take: the exercise UML and the reference solution declare Stock.take(String) to return an int (used to indicate remaining quantity or -1 on failure), while the template implementation declares Stock.take(String) as returning boolean. Specifically: Problem statement (UML) shows +take(String): int; template repository has public boolean take(String ingredient) in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Stock.java; solution repository has public int take(String ingredient) in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Stock.java. A student implementing SealSaloon.checkOrderReady according to the problem description or the solution will expect int semantics (checking for -1 on failure and using returned remaining quantity), but the template's boolean signature and semantics will not match that expectation and will block or confuse correct integration between SealSaloon and Stock.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template Stock.take method match the UML and the solution: change the signature in template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Stock.java to public int take(String ingredient) and implement it to return -1 when the ingredient does not exist or quantity < 1, otherwise decrement the quantity and return the remaining quantity. Alternatively (less recommended), change the problem statement and solution to consistently use boolean semantics, but aligning the template to the existing UML/solution int contract is the clearer fix for students.
